prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 9 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 3 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for CEO's Office; image 2 is the reference sheet for ChatGPT. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: ChatGPT exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: An employee is the red mannequin; Another employee is the blue mannequin; Someone is the yellow mannequin; A manager is the green mannequin; Company A Operations Manager (Employee) is the purple mannequin; Ceo is the orange mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One storyboard image arranged three panels across and three down, read left to right, top to bottom, with equal panels and plain gutters. No panel labels, captions, lettering, numerals or logos are drawn. Daytime, dry conditions and no rain throughout; soft window daylight mixes with cool office illumination in a restrained blue-grey grade. People are smooth, featureless, colour-coded artist's mannequins: red petite and slim, blue tall and slender, yellow short and full-built, green medium-short and stocky, purple medium-height and average-built, orange tall and broad-built. Props and surroundings are painted realistically. The office has pale grey walls, charcoal laminate desks, black chairs, grey visitor chairs, low cabinets, aluminium-framed glazing with horizontal frosted bands, broad roller blinds and grey carpet. Computers have matte black widescreen monitors, compact keyboards and black mice. Application layouts remain distinct, but their writing is replaced by abstract interface marks. The monthly report is a small stack of white printed sheets represented by faint grey blocks without readable characters. The silver compact sedan has right-hand drive, dark grey cloth seats, a black dashboard and lightly tinted windows.

Geography: The route begins at paired workstations in the outer office, continues past the manual spreadsheet desk, and reaches an open internal entrance into the executive room. The same aluminium-framed partition with horizontal frosted bands stays on frame left through these office transitions. Inside, the entrance and standing reporting mark are frame left; the executive desk and seated CEO are frame right. All executive coverage stays on the near side of the employee–CEO axis, preserving purple facing right and orange facing left. The broad window behind the desk occupies frame right and overlooks a distinctive forked, broad-canopy tree beside the office boundary and departure road. That tree remains on frame right through the cut to the car, linking the office view to the beginning of the journey. The car shot is a travel ellipsis outside the suite, with forward travel reading toward screen right; Company B is not yet visible.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Oblique seated-head height, approximately 1.2 metres, from the aisle beside and slightly behind the two workstations. A 35mm two-shot looks diagonally across both desktops, keeping the monitor surfaces visible and both stations in deep focus. Background: The frosted aluminium-framed partition runs along frame left; pale grey wall and low cabinets occupy the upper right. Only this workstation bay is visible: the internal entrance and executive occupants remain outside the frame. Daylight enters from camera left. The red mannequin sits foreground left with chest and head directed toward its monitor at screen right. Its right hand rests on the mouse on the far side of the desktop, partly screened by the forearm, while its left hand lies beside the near edge of the keyboard. The blue mannequin sits farther back at frame right, also with chest and head directed screen right toward its own display, right hand on the far-side mouse and left hand beside the keyboard. The nearer display contains an email pane beside a white assistant conversation with a slim sidebar and rounded input field; the farther display contains a spreadsheet preview beside a separate blue-violet-accented analysis pane.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Oblique desk-level two-shot from the aisle, approximately 1.05 metres high, using a 40mm lens feel. Look across the large monitor at frame left toward the seated worker and standing manager, keeping both readable. Background: The same horizontally frosted partition and aluminium mullion remain at frame left behind the monitor. A pale grey wall and the end of a low document cabinet occupy frame right, giving this desk a different background from the paired workstation bay. The executive room remains concealed. The yellow mannequin sits centre-left in profile, chest and head facing screen left toward a monitor containing two side-by-side spreadsheet grids and one green-outlined cell. Its right hand is visible on the camera-near mouse at lower left, while its left hand rests by the farther edge of the keyboard. The green mannequin stands behind at frame right, chest and head angled screen left, holding the phone with its right hand against the camera-near right side of its head, visible along the head's screen-right outline. Its left arm hangs beside the far hip, partly concealed by the torso.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Wide 35mm view from the near side of the conversational axis, approximately 1.5 metres high. Look across the room with the open entrance at left and executive desk at right, keeping both mannequins and the report clearly visible. Background: The open internal passage and familiar frosted partition occupy frame left. Low cabinets sit behind the desk, while the broad roller-blind window fills the right background; its uncovered lower section reveals the forked broad-canopy tree on frame right. Grey carpet connects the entrance to the desk. The purple mannequin is just inside the entrance at frame left, one foot advanced toward screen right, with chest and head turned toward the orange mannequin across the room. It holds the report at waist height in its left hand on the camera-near side, with the right hand supporting the farther underside. The orange mannequin sits behind the desk at frame right, chest and head facing screen left toward purple, with both hands resting separately on the desktop. Two grey visitor chairs occupy the near side of the desk without obscuring the report.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Waist-up medium single with a 50mm lens feel, at the standing mannequin's head height of approximately 1.6 metres. Camera stays on the master's near side of the axis, giving a three-quarter view directed screen right and leaving space toward the off-frame CEO. Background: The open passage and a vertical mullion of the frosted partition remain on frame left. A narrow area of pale grey executive-room wall fills frame right; the desk window is beyond the right crop. The background is gently soft. The purple mannequin stands at the reporting mark on the left of the composition, chest angled screen right toward the desk and head turned in the same direction. Its left hand bears the report's weight at the camera-near lower edge, while the right hand supports the farther underside. The report sits at waist height along the bottom of the panel, with clear space ahead of the mannequin toward screen right.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Medium close-up with a 65mm lens feel, at seated head height of approximately 1.2 metres. From the same near side of the axis, frame the orange mannequin right of centre in three-quarter orientation toward screen left, with the desk edge low in the picture. Background: The roller-blind window stays on frame right behind the mannequin, with the forked tree softly visible through its lower section. A small area of pale wall and low cabinet occupies frame left; the frosted entrance partition is outside the left crop. The orange mannequin fills the panel from the upper torso upward, chest angled screen left toward the standing employee and head turned toward the same off-frame position. Both hands rest on the desk along the bottom edge, the right hand on the camera-near side and the left hand farther away. Open space is preserved to screen left, in the direction of the employee.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Return to the exact waist-up 50mm employee setup of shot 4, approximately 1.6 metres high. Keep the camera on the near side of the axis and retain the same three-quarter screen-right orientation. Background: The same open passage and frosted-partition mullion remain on frame left, with pale grey wall on frame right. The executive window remains outside the right crop. Background softness and daylight direction match shot 4. The purple mannequin remains standing on the left of the composition, chest facing the desk at screen right and head aligned toward the off-frame orange mannequin. The report stays at waist height, its camera-near edge held by the left hand and its farther underside supported by the right. Both elbows remain close to the torso, leaving the report unobstructed at the bottom of the panel.
PANEL 7 (row 3, column 1) — Return to the exact 65mm medium close-up of shot 5, at seated head height of approximately 1.2 metres. Keep the orange mannequin right of centre, with three-quarter orientation toward screen left and the desk edge at the bottom. Background: The broad window and roller blind remain on frame right, including the softly resolved forked tree below the blind. Pale wall and a small cabinet section remain on frame left. The entrance partition stays beyond the left crop. The orange mannequin sits with chest directed screen left toward the employee and head turned toward that same standing position. Its right hand rests on the camera-near portion of the desktop and its left hand rests farther back, both visible along the lower edge. The composition retains the same open space toward screen left as the earlier desk single.
PANEL 8 (row 3, column 2) — Return to the exact wide 35mm master position of shot 3, approximately 1.5 metres high and on the near side of the axis. Include the employee at the reporting mark, the report and the seated CEO across the desk. Background: The entrance and horizontally frosted glass remain on frame left. The executive window occupies frame right, with the distinctive forked broad-canopy tree visible outside on the same side. Cabinets, visitor chairs and carpet retain their established positions. The purple mannequin now stands with both feet planted at the reporting mark on frame left, chest and head facing screen right toward orange. It retains the report at waist height in the camera-near left hand, supported underneath by the farther right hand. The orange mannequin remains seated frame right with chest and head facing screen left toward purple and both hands resting on the desk. The report is fully visible between them, below their head-to-head line.
PANEL 9 (row 3, column 3) — Passenger-side medium single with a 40mm lens feel, at seated head height of approximately 1.15 metres. The camera sits across the cabin on the left passenger side, slightly behind the driver's shoulder line, showing the driver frame left in three-quarter profile facing screen right, with wheel and lap included. Background: The black dashboard and steering wheel extend toward frame right; a dark grey seat supports the driver at frame left. Through the forward side glass on frame right, the same forked broad-canopy tree is visible beside the office boundary and a straight daytime road. The roadside is softly resolved, dry and free of rain; no destination building is visible. The purple mannequin sits in the right-hand driver's seat, positioned frame left, with chest and head directed forward toward screen right rather than toward the camera. Its right hand reaches to the steering wheel on the far side of the body, visible at lower right. Its left hand holds the report flat against the camera-near thigh at lower centre-left, with the elbow kept beside the torso. The wheel, report and side-on driving posture share the frame.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
